syllabusName: Microeconomics_Kinh t? vi mô
timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
description: Economics is the study of how the society manages its scarce resources. Economics has been divided into the subcategories of microeconomics and macroeconomics. While macroeconomics studies aggregate issues related to national and international economic activities, this course - microeconomics - focuses on the behavior of individual economic agents. Microeconomics studies how households (or individuals), business (or firms, enterprises) and the government make decisions, given scarcity of resources. It also studies the interactions among those market members and how these interactions have impacts on their economic benefits and the economy. Because most of these activities occur in the markets, this course also focuses on how the markets work.

syllabusName: Marketing Principles_Nguyên lý Marketing
timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
description: The course is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in marketing based on five key activities: (1) identifying customer needs, (2) providing customers with the right products or service to meet their needs, (3) assuring availability to customers through the right distribution channels, (4) using promotional activities in ways that motivate purchase as effectively as possible, (5) setting an appropriate price that maximizes firm profitability while maintaining customer satisfaction. The Principle of Marketing course (Philip Kotler) integrates AI tools as supportive instruments for idea generation, document organization, and the practical application of marketing concepts. Students will employ AI for brainstorming, content structuring, creation of marketing materials, and basic analytics, while retaining full responsibility for ensuring originality, critical evaluation, and refinement of their work. The course also equips students to assess the strengths and limitations of AI-generated outputs and to identify ethical risks such as plagiarism and bias. Tools Utilized: - lmarena AI: For generating marketing-related data and insights. - Statista: For accessing statistical data and market research. - ChatGPT: For idea generation, structuring documents, and simulating real-life marketing scenarios. - Canva: For creating visual marketing materials like infographics, templates, and videos. The assessment methods have been reformed to more accurately reflect students’ actual competencies. Learners are evaluated through oral examinations, presentations, group debates, and the assessment of submitted products, as well as through their selection of prompts, which demonstrate their thinking process, revisions, and interactions with AI feedback.

description: This Course is based on the Coursera Specialization "Business Strategy", which covers both the dynamics and the global aspects of strategic management. timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
description: Economics is the study of how the society manages its scarce resources. Economics has been divided into the subcategories of microeconomics and macroeconomics. While macroeconomics studies aggregate issues related to national and international economic activities, this course - microeconomics - focuses on the behavior of individual economic agents. Microeconomics studies how households (or individuals), business (or firms, enterprises) and the government make decisions, given scarcity of resources. It also studies the interactions among those market members and how these interactions have impacts on their economic benefits and the economy. Because most of these activities occur in the markets, this course also focuses on how the markets work.

timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) =82h online + 3h offline + 1h TE + 2h PE + 62 h self-study
description: The course includes two parts:The first part introduces the use of Generative AI (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) in modern software development. Students will learn how AI-powered tools can accelerate the software engineering process, from analyzing requirements to generating code, writing tests, debugging, and producing technical documentation.The second part provides a comprehensive introduction to modern software engineering principles, methods, and practices. The course equips students with the foundational and advanced skills needed to design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain reliable software systems. Learners explore the full software development lifecycle (SDLC), including requirements engineering, architectural and object-oriented design, software construction, quality assurance, and DevOps practices. Emphasis is placed on practical, industry-relevant techniques such as version control, automated testing, API development, and iterative development using Agile. Through a combination of theoretical concepts, hands-on exercises, and real-world case studies, the course prepares students to work effectively in software engineering teams and build scalable, maintainable, and high-quality software products.

syllabusName: Digital Circuit Design_Thi?t k? vi m?ch s?
timeAllocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
description: This course provides students with a solid and comprehensive foundation in digital circuit design. It begins with essential concepts such as number systems, logic gates, Boolean algebra, and logic function simplification. Students then advance to designing and implementing combinational and sequential logic circuits, including multiplexers, arithmetic circuits, flip-flops, shift registers, counters, and memory elements.The course also introduces hardware description languages (VHDL/Verilog), FPGA-based implementation, and fundamental principles of digital signal and data processing. Through these topics, students learn how hardware is described at the Register-Transfer Level (RTL) and how it is verified using testbenches and simulation.In addition, the course provides an overview of the Digital IC Design Flow, including:- Specification and Functional Requirements- RTL Design using HDL- Functional Verification and Testbench Development- Logic Synthesis to Gate-Level Netlist- Timing Analysis and Optimization- Implementation on FPGA or placement & routing (for ASIC)- Post-synthesis simulation and sign-off checksThe module emphasizes not only technical competence but also professional ethics, social responsibility, and the development of creativity and problem-solving skills. Students apply theoretical knowledge through laboratory exercises, hands-on projects, and real-world design practices.

syllabusName: Advanced Game Development_Phát tri?n game nâng cao
timeAllocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
description: This advanced Unity course builds on foundational skills to empower you with expert-level knowledge in creating professional, high-performance games. You'll dive deep into SOLID principles and design patterns for writing clean, scalable code, while mastering Unity's networking tools and cloud services to build engaging multiplayer experiences. Hands-on projects will help you optimize performance, integrate AI, and deliver polished games ready for consoles, PC, and beyond.Key Learning Outcomes: - Master SOLID Principles: Build a solid grasp of the five SOLID principles (Single Responsibility, Open-Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, and Dependency Inversion) and apply them to make your Unity code more modular and easier to maintain. - Implement Design Patterns: Get hands-on with essential Unity patterns like Singleton, Observer, Command, Strategy, Factory, Decorator, and State to organize code, boost flexibility, and simplify complex game logic. - Build with Unity Networking: Explore Unity Relay and Netcode to design smooth, reliable multiplayer systems that handle real-time interactions effortlessly. - Integrate Unity Gaming Services: Use cloud tools like Player Authentication, Lobbies, In-Game Economy, and Leaderboards to add secure, scalable features that enhance player engagement. - Optimize Performance: Discover profiling techniques and best practices to fine-tune your games for buttery-smooth gameplay, reduced lag, and efficient resource use on various devices. - Create Multiplayer Games: Develop small real-time multiplayer prototypes using Unity's networking and collaboration tools, following industry-standard workflows. - Leverage Unity AI: Incorporate AI models via Unity Sentis or similar tools to add intelligent behaviors, like smart NPCs or procedural content, to your game projects.By the end of this course, you'll have the confidence and skills to solve tough game development problems, from code architecture to live multiplayer features, and produce professional-quality games with cutting-edge design and tech.
